visa_types.notes: Official electronic visa system launched by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, applied for via evisa.gov.tr; used for short-term tourism and trade/business visits, not valid for work or study.

Issued under Law No. 6458 to foreigners staying beyond the 90-day visa/e-Visa limit for purposes such as tourism, property ownership, or other short-term reasons; administered via e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr.
Issued to foreigners enrolled in higher education or accredited programs at Turkish institutions, per the DGMM's official residence-permit-types page.
Granted to spouses and dependent children of Turkish citizens or of foreigners holding a valid residence/work permit, per the official DGMM page.
Regulated by Articles 41-42 of Law No. 6458, granted after continuous lawful residence (commonly cited as 8 years), listed on the official DGMM residence-permit-types page.

Regulated by Articles 46-47 of Law No. 6458, per the official DGMM page. Classified here as closest to family_reunion/other since it doesn't fit the standard purpose set cleanly; it's a humanitarian protection-related permit, not tied to work, study, tourism, business, or standard PR.
One of the standard work permit types issued by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security under International Labour Force Law No. 6735; substitutes for a residence permit.
Available to foreigners with 8 years of legal residence/work in Turkey, per the Ministry of Labour's official work-permit-types page.
For self-employed foreigners, evaluated based on education, professional experience, and economic contribution, per the official Ministry of Labour page.

A distinct work-permit category for highly qualified foreigners (based on education, experience, investment impact); grants rights similar to a permanent work permit. Confirmed on the official Ministry of Labour work-permit-types page.
